Ui.Script:
-- ── What a coin is worth ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- Published globals: an addon that formats a price does the same split we do below, and -- reads these rather than spelling 100 twice. COPPER_PER_SILVER = 100 SILVER_PER_GOLD = 100 COPPER_PER_GOLD = COPPER_PER_SILVER * SILVER_PER_GOLD
-- ── How wide a coin draws ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- One coin icon's width at each of the two sizes the templates below come in, and the gap -- between two coin buttons — NEGATIVE, because the three deliberately bite into each other -- so a group reads as one number rather than as three. `COIN_BUTTON_WIDTH` is the fixed slot -- a `fixedWidth` type pads its smaller coins out to, so a column of prices lines up. -- The values are the specification's (ref l.2-12): measurements of the shipped coin art, not -- ours to re-derive. MONEY_ICON_WIDTH = 19 MONEY_ICON_WIDTH_SMALL = 13 MONEY_BUTTON_SPACING = -4 MONEY_BUTTON_SPACING_SMALL = -4 COIN_BUTTON_WIDTH = 32
-- ── The money types (ref l.14-103) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- A money frame carries no amount of its own: it carries a TYPE, and the type says where the -- number comes from and how the coins behave. An entry has three parts: -- -- · `UpdateFunc()` returns the amount, in copper. It is called with the global `this` bound -- to the frame being painted, so a type may read the frame as well as the engine. -- · `PickupFunc(amount)` / `DropFunc()` are the cursor verbs a click-to-pick-up type drives. -- · the display flags `MoneyFrame_Update` reads: `collapse` (drop leading zero -- denominations), `showSmallerCoins` (keep the trailing ones on even at zero; the value -- "Backpack" additionally keeps copper on by itself), `canPickup` (the coins take the -- mouse), `fixedWidth` (pad the smaller coins to COIN_BUTTON_WIDTH), `truncateSmallCoins` -- (drop copper once there is gold). -- -- Nothing else is consulted. That is why those field names and the two function signatures -- are the published contract and not an implementation detail: addons register types of their -- own into this table and expect exactly these parts to be honoured. MoneyTypeInfo = { }
-- Read an amount through an engine verb that may not be built here yet: absent, it reads 0 -- rather than calling into nil. Two of the seven types below need it — see the header. local function AmountFrom(verbName) local verb = getglobal(verbName) if verb then return verb() end return 0 end
-- The purse. The specification subtracts a third term here (ref l.17, -- `GetMoney() - GetCursorMoney() - GetPlayerTradeMoney()`): coins lifted onto the cursor by -- the coin-pickup frame. benilla ships neither that frame nor the `PickupPlayerMoney` verb -- behind it, so the term is structurally 0 rather than approximated away — it comes back the -- moment either lands. MoneyTypeInfo["PLAYER"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return GetMoney() - GetPlayerTradeMoney() end, PickupFunc = function(amount) PickupPlayerMoney(amount) end, DropFunc = function() DropCursorMoney() end, collapse = 1, canPickup = 1, showSmallerCoins = "Backpack", }
-- A number the owner parked on the frame itself — what `MoneyFrame_Update(name, amount)` -- leaves behind, and how an addon shows a price it worked out for itself. MoneyTypeInfo["STATIC"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return this.staticMoney end, collapse = 1, }
-- The auction house's price column: the same source as STATIC, but the smaller coins pad out -- to a fixed slot and stay on at zero, so a stack of prices reads as a column of digits. MoneyTypeInfo["AUCTION"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return this.staticMoney end, collapse = 1, showSmallerCoins = "Backpack", fixedWidth = 1, truncateSmallCoins = nil, }
-- Our side of an open trade, and the other party's. Only ours is click-to-pick-up. MoneyTypeInfo["PLAYER_TRADE"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return GetPlayerTradeMoney() end, PickupFunc = function(amount) PickupTradeMoney(amount) end, DropFunc = function() AddTradeMoney() end, collapse = 1, canPickup = 1, }
MoneyTypeInfo["TARGET_TRADE"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return GetTargetTradeMoney() end, collapse = 1, }
-- Mail postage and cash-on-delivery. Postage explicitly does NOT collapse (ref l.84): the -- send-mail frame wants all three coins standing whatever the amount, because you are typing -- into them. Both read 0 until their engine getters exist — see the header. MoneyTypeInfo["SEND_MAIL"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return AmountFrom("GetSendMailMoney") end, PickupFunc = function(amount) PickupSendMailMoney(amount) end, DropFunc = function() AddSendMailMoney() end, collapse = nil, canPickup = 1, showSmallerCoins = "Backpack", }
MoneyTypeInfo["SEND_MAIL_COD"] = { UpdateFunc = function() return AmountFrom("GetSendMailCOD") end, PickupFunc = function(amount) PickupSendMailCOD(amount) end, DropFunc = function() AddSendMailCOD() end, collapse = 1, canPickup = 1, }
-- ── Hearing about a change (ref l.105-140) ─────────────────────────────────────────────── -- -- Every money frame registers all five money events; each then decides whether the one that -- arrived is about the number IT is showing. That pairing is data, not control flow, so it is -- written as data: one row per event, in the order the templates register them, naming the -- money types that event can change. local MONEY_EVENTS = { { "PLAYER_MONEY", { PLAYER = 1 } }, { "PLAYER_TRADE_MONEY", { PLAYER = 1, PLAYER_TRADE = 1 } }, { "TRADE_MONEY_CHANGED", { TARGET_TRADE = 1 } }, { "SEND_MAIL_MONEY_CHANGED", { PLAYER = 1, SEND_MAIL = 1 } }, { "SEND_MAIL_COD_CHANGED", { PLAYER = 1, SEND_MAIL_COD = 1 } }, }
-- The same rows keyed by event name, built once, so the handler below is a lookup. local moneyEventTypes = { } for _, row in ipairs(MONEY_EVENTS) do moneyEventTypes[row[1]] = row[2] end
local function MoneyFrameListen(frame) for _, row in ipairs(MONEY_EVENTS) do frame:RegisterEvent(row[1]) end end
-- The two OnLoads differ in exactly one thing: `small`, which is what picks the 13px coin and -- its tighter spacing over the 19px one in MoneyFrame_Update below. Both then take type -- PLAYER, so a frame nobody tells otherwise shows the purse. function MoneyFrame_OnLoad() MoneyFrameListen(this) MoneyFrame_SetType("PLAYER") end
function SmallMoneyFrame_OnLoad() MoneyFrameListen(this) this.small = 1 MoneyFrame_SetType("PLAYER") end
function MoneyFrame_OnEvent() if not this.info or not this:IsVisible() then return end local affected = moneyEventTypes[event] if affected and affected[this.moneyType] then MoneyFrame_UpdateMoney() end end
-- ── Painting ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-- A money frame's three coin buttons, biggest first. Every verb below addresses them as a -- trio, so this is the one place their `$parent<Denomination>Button` names are spelled. local function MoneyFrameCoins(frameName) return getglobal(frameName .. "GoldButton"), getglobal(frameName .. "SilverButton"), getglobal(frameName .. "CopperButton") end
-- Point a frame at a money type (ref l.142-162): remember it, wire the mouse to match, and -- repaint. Reads `this` rather than taking a frame — that is the convention the eleven corpus -- callers write against. function MoneyFrame_SetType(type) local info = MoneyTypeInfo[type] if not info then -- ref l.145 diagnoses this with `message()`, which we do not ship (see the header). if message then message("Invalid money type: " .. type) end return end this.info = info this.moneyType = type -- Only a click-to-pick-up type wants the mouse; on the rest a click falls through to -- whatever is behind the coins. local gold, silver, copper = MoneyFrameCoins(this:GetName()) local pickable = info.canPickup and true or false gold:EnableMouse(pickable) silver:EnableMouse(pickable) copper:EnableMouse(pickable) MoneyFrame_UpdateMoney() end
-- Re-read the amount from the type and repaint (ref l.164-175). `this` again. function MoneyFrame_UpdateMoney() if not this.info then if message then message("Error moneyType not set") end return end local money = this.info.UpdateFunc() MoneyFrame_Update(this:GetName(), money) -- ref l.169-171 also feeds the coin-pickup frame while one is open. `hasPickup` is set -- only by the coin click, which is guarded off (see the header), so this is unreachable -- today rather than removed. if this.hasPickup == 1 and UpdateCoinPickupFrame then UpdateCoinPickupFrame(money) end end
-- Lay one denomination out: its digits, and the width those digits plus the coin icon need. -- -- `Button:GetTextWidth()` right after `SetText`, which is what the specification writes -- (ref l.202 and kin) and what the real client answers synchronously off its inline font -- engine, so the coin is the right width on the frame that set its text. -- -- This read used to return 0 — our measure landed at extract, a frame after the tick — and -- left all three coins at exactly one bare icon width with their digits overlapping: the -- director's "gold numbers are all cramped up when I first open the bags; close and open -- again and it looks good", the reopen being the first open's cached measure. It was served -- for a while by a digits-only advance table, since a number's width is a pure sum of -- per-glyph advances. The engine answers the general question now (`script::measure`), so -- this asks it the way the specification does. local function ShowCoin(coin, coinName, amount, iconWidth) coin:SetText(amount) coin:SetWidth(coin:GetTextWidth() + iconWidth) coin:Show() end
-- Chain the next-bigger coin onto `coin`, and report what `coin` contributes to the group's -- width. -- -- Showing: the bigger coin hangs off this one's LEFT edge by `spacing` (negative — they -- overlap), and the group grows by this coin's width less that overlap, but only when the -- bigger coin is actually on screen to overlap with. Not showing: this coin hides and the -- bigger one collapses onto its RIGHT edge, contributing nothing. `padToSlot` is the -- `fixedWidth` exception, which sizes the coin to the fixed column slot first. local function ChainCoin(bigger, coin, coinName, showing, padToSlot, spacing) if not showing then coin:Hide() bigger:SetPoint("RIGHT", coinName, "RIGHT", 0, 0) return 0 end if padToSlot then coin:SetWidth(COIN_BUTTON_WIDTH) end local grown = coin:GetWidth() bigger:SetPoint("RIGHT", coinName, "LEFT", spacing, 0) if bigger:IsVisible() then grown = grown - spacing end return grown end
-- THE PAINTER (ref l.177-270). Split a copper amount into the three denominations, size each -- coin to its own digits plus its icon, and then — if the type collapses — drop the leading -- zeros, re-chain what is left so the group packs tight, and report the frame's true width. -- -- This one takes a frame NAME, not `this`: it is the only entry point in the family an owner -- can call about a frame other than the one currently dispatching, which is how an addon -- paints a STATIC frame it has just filled. function MoneyFrame_Update(frameName, money) local frame = getglobal(frameName) local info = frame.info if not info then -- ref l.181 diagnoses and, notably, does NOT return: the coins below are still laid -- out, and the collapse read further down is what actually stops it. Kept as-is. if message then message("Error moneyType not set") end end
-- Copper is the low two digits, silver the next two, gold everything above. Silver comes -- out by subtracting the gold back off rather than by a second `mod`: `mod` here is 1.12's -- `math.mod`, which truncates towards zero, so `mod(-1, 100)` is -1 and not 99 — the two -- forms part company the moment `money` goes negative (which `GetMoney()` minus a trade -- offer can), and this one is the specified answer. -- A STATIC/AUCTION frame's amount is whatever its owner last parked on it, and on the -- very first paint — `MoneyFrame_SetType`'s own repaint, in OnLoad, before any owner has -- filled it — that is nil. The specification divides straight into it and throws there; -- we answer 0, because the throw would take the whole `<OnLoad>`/`<OnShow>` chain down -- with it and an empty price column is the honest reading of "nothing set yet". money = money or 0 local gold = floor(money / COPPER_PER_GOLD) local silver = floor((money - gold * COPPER_PER_GOLD) / COPPER_PER_SILVER) local copper = mod(money, COPPER_PER_SILVER)
local goldCoin, silverCoin, copperCoin = MoneyFrameCoins(frameName) local iconWidth, spacing = MONEY_ICON_WIDTH, MONEY_BUTTON_SPACING if frame.small then iconWidth, spacing = MONEY_ICON_WIDTH_SMALL, MONEY_BUTTON_SPACING_SMALL end
ShowCoin(goldCoin, frameName .. "GoldButton", gold, iconWidth) ShowCoin(silverCoin, frameName .. "SilverButton", silver, iconWidth) ShowCoin(copperCoin, frameName .. "CopperButton", copper, iconWidth)
-- Remember what the frame is displaying — STATIC's own reader reads it back. frame.staticMoney = money
-- A type that does not collapse is finished: all three coins stand, at the width their -- digits asked for, and the frame keeps whatever width it was given. if not info.collapse then return end
-- Gold leads. Present, it stays and sets the terms for the two below it; absent, it goes. -- The running width starts at one icon's worth of frame padding. local width = iconWidth local keepSmaller, dropCopper if gold > 0 then width = width + goldCoin:GetWidth() keepSmaller = info.showSmallerCoins and 1 or nil dropCopper = info.truncateSmallCoins and 1 or nil else goldCoin:Hide() end
-- Silver, then copper: each either shows — padded, chained and counted — or hides and lets -- the coin above it collapse onto its edge. Silver showing under a `showSmallerCoins` type -- is what carries the exemption down to copper; copper also survives at zero for a -- "Backpack" type, and dies whatever it is once gold truncated it. local showSilver = silver > 0 or keepSmaller width = width + ChainCoin(goldCoin, silverCoin, frameName .. "SilverButton", showSilver, keepSmaller and info.fixedWidth, spacing) if showSilver and info.showSmallerCoins then keepSmaller = 1 end
local showCopper = (copper > 0 or keepSmaller or info.showSmallerCoins == "Backpack") and not dropCopper width = width + ChainCoin(silverCoin, copperCoin, frameName .. "CopperButton", showCopper, keepSmaller and info.fixedWidth, spacing)
frame:SetWidth(width) end
-- A NO-OP, deliberately. The specification's whole body for this one sits inside a `--[[ ]]` -- block (ref l.272-346) — an earlier painter that MoneyFrame_Update replaced. The name is in -- the shipped client's `_G`, and an addon that calls it there gets exactly this: nothing. function RefreshMoneyFrame(frameName, money, small, collapse, showSmallerCoins) end
-- Recolour the DIGITS; the coin icons keep their own texture (ref l.348-356). This is how a -- price you cannot afford turns red. function SetMoneyFrameColor(frameName, r, g, b) local gold, silver, copper = MoneyFrameCoins(frameName) gold:SetTextColor(r, g, b) silver:SetTextColor(r, g, b) copper:SetTextColor(r, g, b) end
-- A click on a coin opens the pickup frame on that denomination, seeded with what the frame is -- currently showing; `denomination` is one coin's worth in copper, which is the unit the -- pickup frame counts in. -- -- Guarded, because we ship no coin pickup (see the header) — so today the click does nothing, -- and the mouse-enabled state a `canPickup` type gives the coins is all that is observable. -- Note the amount is read by calling the type's own `UpdateFunc` while `this` is still the -- BUTTON rather than the frame, which is what the specification's own coin `<OnClick>` does -- (ref MoneyFrame.xml l.20-23) and what a frame-reading type would see through. function BenillaMoneyFrameCoin_OnClick(coin, denomination) if not OpenCoinPickupFrame then return end local frame = coin:GetParent() OpenCoinPickupFrame(denomination, MoneyTypeInfo[frame.moneyType].UpdateFunc(), frame) frame.hasPickup = 1 end
-- Closing a money frame takes any pickup it opened down with it. function BenillaMoneyFrame_OnHide() if this.hasPickup == 1 and CoinPickupFrame then CoinPickupFrame:Hide() this.hasPickup = 0 end end
